title: Alternating Current
syllabus: Alternating currents, Peak and RMS value of alternating current/voltage; Reactance and impedance; LCR series circuit, Resonance; Power in AC circuits, Wattless current; AC generator and transformer.

questions.question: A series LCR circuit with $R = 20\,\Omega$, $L = 1.5\text{ H}$ and $C = 35\text{ \mu F}$ is connected to a variable-frequency $200\text{ V}$ ac supply. When the frequency of the supply equals the natural frequency of the circuit, what is the average power transferred to the circuit in one complete cycle? (NEET 2022)
questions.solution:
At resonance, the inductive and capacitive reactances cancel each other ($X_L = X_C$), so the impedance of the circuit is purely resistive: $Z = R = 20\,\Omega$.
RMS current at resonance: $I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{V_{\text{rms}}}{Z} = \frac{200\text{ V}}{20\,\Omega} = 10\text{ A}$.
Power factor $\cos\phi = 1$.
Average power dissipated: $P_{\text{avg}} = V_{\text{rms}} I_{\text{rms}} \cos\phi = 200 \times 10 \times 1 = 2000\text{ W}$.

questions.question: An inductor of inductance $L$, a capacitor of capacitance $C$ and a resistor of resistance $R$ are connected in series to an ac source of potential difference $V$ volts as shown in the figure. The potential differences across $L$, $C$ and $R$ are $40\text{ V}$, $10\text{ V}$ and $40\text{ V}$, respectively. The amplitude of the voltage of the ac source $V$ is: (NEET 2021)
questions.solution:
The RMS value of the net voltage across the series LCR circuit is:
$$V_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2} = \sqrt{40^2 + (40 - 10)^2} = \sqrt{40^2 + 30^2} = \sqrt{1600 + 900} = 50\text{ V}$$
The peak value (amplitude) of the source voltage is:
$$V_0 = \sqrt{2} V_{\text{rms}} = 50\sqrt{2}\text{ V}$$

questions.question: The peak voltage of the ac source is equal to: (NEET 2020)
options: $\sqrt{2}$ times the rms value of the ac source
The rms value of the ac source
$\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ times the rms value of the ac source
$2$ times the rms value of the ac source
questions.solution: For a sinusoidal alternating voltage, $V_{\text{rms}} = \frac{V_0}{\sqrt{2}} \implies V_0 = \sqrt{2} V_{\text{rms}}$. Thus, the peak voltage is $\sqrt{2}$ times the RMS voltage.

questions.question: A $44\text{ mH}$ inductor is connected to $220\text{ V}, 50\text{ Hz}$ ac supply. The rms value of the current in the circuit is: (NEET 2020)
questions.solution:
Inductive reactance: $X_L = 2\pi f L = 2 \times 3.1416 \times 50 \times (44 \times 10^{-3}) = 13.82\,\Omega$.
$$I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{V_{\text{rms}}}{X_L} = \frac{220\text{ V}}{13.82\,\Omega} \approx 15.92\text{ A} \approx 15.9\text{ A}$$

questions.question: A step-down transformer connected to an ac mains supply of $220\text{ V}$ is made to operate at $11\text{ V}, 44\text{ W}$ lamp. Ignoring power losses in the transformer, what is the current in the primary circuit? (NEET 2021)
questions.solution:
For an ideal transformer (zero power loss): $P_{\text{in}} = P_{\text{out}} = 44\text{ W}$.
$$V_p I_p = P_{\text{out}} \implies 220 \times I_p = 44 \implies I_p = \frac{44}{220} = 0.2\text{ A}$$

questions.question: An alternating current is given by the equation $i = i_1\cos\omega t + i_2\sin\omega t$. The rms value of current is: (NEET 2016)
questions.solution:
The net amplitude of the resultant harmonic current is $i_0 = \sqrt{i_1^2 + i_2^2}$.
$$i_{\text{rms}} = \frac{i_0}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{i_1^2 + i_2^2}{2}}$$

questions.question: A small signal voltage $V(t) = V_0\sin\omega t$ is applied across an ideal capacitor $C$. Over a complete cycle, the capacitor: (NEET 2016)
options: Does not consume any energy from the voltage source
Consumes energy at a constant rate
questions.solution:
In a purely capacitive circuit, current leads voltage by a phase angle of $90^\circ$ ($\phi = \pi/2$).
The power factor is $\cos\phi = \cos 90^\circ = 0$, so average power consumed over a complete cycle is $P_{\text{avg}} = V_{\text{rms}} I_{\text{rms}} \cos 90^\circ = 0$.

questions.question: The phase difference between alternating current and voltage in a purely inductive ac circuit is:
options: Current and voltage are in phase
questions.solution: In a pure inductor, the back EMF opposes current growth, causing alternating current to lag behind alternating voltage by a phase difference of $\frac{\pi}{2}\text{ rad}$ ($90^\circ$).

questions.question: The resonant frequency $\omega_0$ of a series LCR circuit having inductance $L$ and capacitance $C$ is:
questions.solution: At resonance: $X_L = X_C \implies \omega_0 L = \frac{1}{\omega_0 C} \implies \omega_0^2 = \frac{1}{LC} \implies \omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$.

questions.question: A wattless current flows through an ac circuit when the phase difference between current and voltage is:
questions.solution: Average power is $P = V_{\text{rms}} I_{\text{rms}} \cos\phi$. When $\phi = \frac{\pi}{2}$ ($90^\circ$), $\cos\phi = 0$, so no power is dissipated in the circuit and the current is termed wattless.

questions.question: The primary and secondary coils of a transformer have 500 and 5000 turns respectively. If the primary is connected to a $200\text{ V}, 50\text{ Hz}$ ac supply, the secondary output voltage and frequency are:
questions.solution:
Voltage ratio: $\frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \implies V_s = 200 \times \frac{5000}{500} = 2000\text{ V}$.
A transformer changes voltage and current levels without altering the supply frequency ($f = 50\text{ Hz}$).

questions.question: In a series LCR circuit, the voltage across $R, L,$ and $C$ are $V_R = 80\text{ V}, V_L = 100\text{ V},$ and $V_C = 40\text{ V}$. The power factor of the circuit is:
questions.solution:
Total circuit voltage $V = \sqrt{V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2} = \sqrt{80^2 + (100 - 40)^2} = \sqrt{6400 + 3600} = 100\text{ V}$.
$$\text{Power factor } \cos\phi = \frac{V_R}{V} = \frac{80}{100} = 0.8$$

questions.question: An alternating current is given by $i = 10\sqrt{2}\sin(100\pi t)\text{ A}$. The frequency and the rms value of the current are:
questions.solution:
Peak current $i_0 = 10\sqrt{2}\text{ A} \implies i_{\text{rms}} = \frac{i_0}{\sqrt{2}} = 10\text{ A}$.
Angular frequency $\omega = 100\pi = 2\pi f \implies f = 50\text{ Hz}$.

questions.question: If the frequency of an ac supply in a purely capacitive circuit is doubled, the capacitive reactance of the circuit will:
questions.solution: Capacitive reactance is $X_C = \frac{1}{2\pi f C} \propto \frac{1}{f}$. When frequency is doubled ($f' = 2f$), $X_C' = X_C / 2$.

questions.question: A capacitor blocks direct current (DC) because for DC:
questions.solution: For steady DC, frequency is zero ($f = 0$). Thus, capacitive reactance $X_C = \frac{1}{2\pi f C} = \frac{1}{0} = \infty$, presenting infinite opposition and blocking DC completely.

questions.question: The quality factor ($Q$-factor) of a series resonant LCR circuit is given by:
questions.solution: $$Q = \frac{\omega_0 L}{R} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}\left(\frac{L}{R}\right) = \frac{1}{R}\sqrt{\frac{L}{C}}$$

questions.question: An ac source of $e = 220\sin(100t)\text{ V}$ is connected across a resistor of $44\,\Omega$. The current reading in an ordinary AC ammeter connected in the circuit is:
questions.solution:
Peak current $I_0 = \frac{V_0}{R} = \frac{220}{44} = 5\text{ A}$.
An AC ammeter measures the RMS value of current:
$$I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\text{ A}$$

questions.question: In an ac circuit, $V = 100\sin(100t)\text{ V}$ and $I = 100\sin\left(100t + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)\text{ mA}$. The power consumed in the circuit is:
questions.solution: $$P_{\text{avg}} = \frac{1}{2} V_0 I_0 \cos\phi = \frac{1}{2} \times 100 \times (100 \times 10^{-3}) \times \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 0.5 = 2.5\text{ W}$$

questions.question: The core of a transformer is laminated to minimize energy loss due to:
questions.solution: Lamination of the iron core into thin sheets separated by insulating layers increases the electrical resistance across transverse loop paths, effectively minimizing eddy current losses.

questions.question: A coil of resistance $30\,\Omega$ and inductive reactance $40\,\Omega$ is connected to a $100\text{ V}$ ac supply. The impedance of the coil is:
In a series LCR circuit connected to an alternating voltage source, if $X_L > X_C$, the phase relationship is:
options: Current lags voltage by angle $\phi = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{X_L - X_C}{R}\right)$
Current leads voltage by angle $\phi = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{X_L - X_C}{R}\right)$
Current and voltage are in phase
questions.solution: When $X_L > X_C$, the circuit is predominantly inductive, so the alternating current lags behind the source voltage by phase angle $\phi = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{X_L - X_C}{R}\right)$.

questions.question: An ac generator consists of a coil of 100 turns and cross-sectional area $0.1\text{ m}^2$ rotating at $3000\text{ rpm}$ in a uniform magnetic field of $0.05\text{ T}$. The peak value of induced emf is:
questions.solution:
Angular speed $\omega = 3000 \times \frac{2\pi}{60} = 100\pi\text{ rad/s}$.
$$\varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = 100 \times 0.05 \times 0.1 \times 100\pi = 50\pi\text{ V}$$

questions.question: The mean (average) value of sinusoidal alternating current over a positive half-cycle ($0$ to $T/2$) is:
questions.solution: $$I_{\text{avg}} = \frac{1}{T/2}\int_0^{T/2} I_0\sin(\omega t)\,dt = \frac{2I_0}{\pi} \approx 0.637 I_0$$

questions.question: The mean (average) value of sinusoidal alternating current over one complete cycle ($0$ to $T$) is:
questions.solution: Over a full cycle, positive and negative half-cycles are symmetrical and cancel each other completely, giving an average value of zero.

questions.question: A choke coil is preferred over a rheostat to reduce current in an AC circuit because:
options: It has high inductance and low resistance, minimizing power wastage
It consumes power at a constant rate
It increases the power factor to unity
It completely blocks high frequency ac
questions.solution: An ideal choke coil has large inductance $L$ and nearly zero resistance $R$. Its power factor $\cos\phi \approx 0$, so it controls AC current through inductive reactance ($X_L = \omega L$) with negligible Joule heating power loss.

questions.question: In a series LCR circuit, sharpness of resonance increases when:
questions.solution: Sharpness of resonance is measured by the $Q$-factor: $Q = \frac{1}{R}\sqrt{\frac{L}{C}}$. Decreasing resistance $R$ narrows the bandwidth ($\Delta\omega = R/L$), making the resonance curve sharper.

questions.question: An alternating voltage $V = 141.4\sin(100\pi t)\text{ V}$ is applied across a $10\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitor. The rms current in the circuit is:
questions.solution:
$$V_{\text{rms}} = \frac{V_0}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{141.4}{1.414} = 100\text{ V}$$
$$X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} = \frac{1}{100\pi \times 10 \times 10^{-6}} = \frac{10^3}{\pi}\,\Omega$$
$$I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{V_{\text{rms}}}{X_C} = \frac{100}{1000/\pi} = 0.1\pi \approx 0.314\text{ A}$$

questions.question: A transformer has an efficiency of $80\%$ and operates on $4\text{ kW}$ and $100\text{ V}$. If the secondary voltage is $200\text{ V}$, the primary and secondary currents are:
questions.solution:
Input power: $P_{\text{in}} = V_p I_p = 4000\text{ W} \implies 100 \times I_p = 4000 \implies I_p = 40\text{ A}$.
Output power: $P_{\text{out}} = 0.80 \times 4000 = 3200\text{ W}$.
$$V_s I_s = 3200 \implies 200 \times I_s = 3200 \implies I_s = 16\text{ A}$$

questions.question: In a series LR circuit, $R = 10\,\Omega$ and $L = 0.1\text{ H}$. When connected to a $50\text{ Hz}$ ac supply, the phase angle between voltage and current is:
questions.solution:
$$X_L = 2\pi f L = 2\pi (50)(0.1) = 10\pi\,\Omega$$
$$\tan\phi = \frac{X_L}{R} = \frac{10\pi}{10} = \pi \implies \phi = \tan^{-1}(\pi)$$

questions.question: An ideal transformer cannot step up or step down:
questions.solution: Transformers operate on the principle of mutual induction driven by changing magnetic flux. Direct current (DC) creates a static magnetic field ($\frac{d\Phi}{dt} = 0$), producing zero induced secondary voltage.

questions.question: The dimensional formula of inductive reactance $X_L$ and capacitive reactance $X_C$ is identical to that of:
questions.solution: Reactance represents opposition to AC current flow ($X = V/I$) and is measured in ohms ($\Omega$), sharing the dimensional formula of resistance: $[\text{M}\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-3}\text{A}^{-2}]$.

questions.question: In a series LCR circuit, at resonant frequency $\omega_0$, the impedance $Z$ is:
questions.solution: At resonance, $X_L = X_C$, so impedance $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2} = R$, which is the minimum possible impedance, resulting in maximum current amplitude.

questions.question: A $100\,\Omega$ iron core inductor is connected across a $220\text{ V}, 50\text{ Hz}$ supply. If the iron core is withdrawn from the inductor, the current in the circuit will:
questions.solution: Removing the high-permeability iron core decreases the inductance ($L \downarrow$), which decreases the inductive reactance ($X_L = 2\pi f L \downarrow$). Total impedance decreases, causing current $I = V/Z$ to increase.

questions.question: If an alternating current of peak value $I_0$ passes through a pure resistor $R$, the heat produced in time $t$ ($t \gg T$) is:
questions.solution: $$H = I_{\text{rms}}^2 R t = \left(\frac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 R t = \frac{1}{2} I_0^2 R t$$

questions.question: The power factor of a purely resistive circuit is:
questions.solution:
In a purely resistive circuit, current and voltage are in phase ($\phi = 0^\circ$).
$$\text{Power factor } \cos\phi = \cos 0^\circ = 1$$

questions.question: A series LCR circuit has $L = 10\text{ mH}$, $C = 1\text{ \mu F}$, and $R = 10\,\Omega$. The resonant angular frequency is:
In a step-up transformer, the transformation ratio $k = N_s / N_p$ is:
questions.solution: A step-up transformer increases voltage ($V_s > V_p$), which requires a greater number of turns in the secondary coil ($N_s > N_p$), so $k = N_s / N_p > 1$.

questions.question: When a direct current $I_{\text{dc}}$ and an alternating current of peak value $I_0$ produce heat in identical resistors at the same rate, then:
questions.solution: By definition, the RMS value of AC is the equivalent DC current that produces heat at the exact same rate in a given resistor: $I_{\text{dc}} = I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}$.

questions.question: In an LCR series circuit, if the capacitance is made 4 times its initial value, what should be the new inductance to keep the resonant frequency unchanged?
questions.solution:
Since $\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$, the product $L C$ must remain constant.
$$L' C' = L C \implies L'(4C) = L C \implies L' = \frac{L}{4}$$

questions.question: A capacitor of capacitive reactance $30\,\Omega$ and a resistor of $40\,\Omega$ are connected in series across an AC source. The impedance of the circuit is:
The wattless component of current in an AC circuit having current $I_{\text{rms}}$ and phase difference $\phi$ with voltage is:
questions.solution: Current resolves into an active (in-phase) component $I_{\text{rms}}\cos\phi$ and a reactive (quadrature, out-of-phase by $90^\circ$) component $I_{\text{rms}}\sin\phi$, which consumes zero average power and is termed wattless current.

questions.question: Copper loss in a transformer is caused by:
options: Joule heating in the primary and secondary copper windings
Induced eddy currents in the iron core
Periodic reversal of magnetization in the core
questions.solution: Copper loss ($I^2 R$ loss) refers to the electrical power dissipated as heat in the internal resistance of the copper wire windings carrying primary and secondary currents.

questions.question: An alternating current is represented as $i = 6\sin(100\pi t) + 8\cos(100\pi t)\text{ A}$. The rms value of current is:
questions.solution:
Resultant peak amplitude: $I_0 = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{36 + 64} = 10\text{ A}$.
$$I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{10}{\sqrt{2}}\text{ A} = 5\sqrt{2}\text{ A}$$

questions.question: In an AC circuit with voltage $V$ and current $I$, the apparent power and true power are related by:
questions.solution: Apparent power is $V_{\text{rms}} I_{\text{rms}}$, while true (active) power is $P = V_{\text{rms}} I_{\text{rms}} \cos\phi = \text{Apparent Power} \times \cos\phi$.

questions.question: A series LCR circuit has $R = 10\,\Omega$, $X_L = 100\,\Omega$, and $X_C = 100\,\Omega$. When connected to a $200\text{ V}, 50\text{ Hz}$ supply, the current flowing in the circuit is:
questions.solution:
Since $X_L = X_C = 100\,\Omega$, the circuit is in resonance ($Z = R = 10\,\Omega$).
$$I = \frac{V}{Z} = \frac{200\text{ V}}{10\,\Omega} = 20\text{ A}$$
